sanskrit_verse:
प्रायश्चित्तमकुर्वाणाः पापेषु निरता नराः ।
अपश्चात्तापिनः कष्टान् नरकान्यान्ति दारुणान् ॥३.२२१॥
transliteration: prāyaścittam akurvāṇāḥ pāpeṣu niratā narāḥ | apaścāttāpinaḥ kaṣṭān narakān yānti dāruṇān ||3.221||
sph_interpretive_translation: Those who remain engaged in sin without performing prāyaścitta, and who lack subsequent remorse, enter harsh and painful realms of existence due to their own karmic alignment.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority: Karmic consequence is self-executing and independent of external judgment.
Causation: Engagement in harmful action without corrective intent generates binding karmic sequences.
Capacity-based responsibility: Responsibility arises from conscious choice and awareness, not mere occurrence.
Restoration logic: Consequence serves as a mechanism for experiential realignment with Dharma.
Consciousness alignment: Suffering occurs when consciousness is misaligned with its inherent purity.
executable_legal_axioms: IF an individual engages in harmful conduct AND does not initiate prāyaścitta within one lunar cycle THEN automatic karmic consequence protocol initiates.
IF consciousness misalignment is detected through behavioral pattern analysis THEN assign experiential correction pathway.
IF no remorse signal is registered post-action THEN escalate to higher-intensity experiential learning loop.
IF prāyaścitta is completed authentically THEN terminate karmic feedback sequence immediately.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, the threshold of responsibility includes both actus reus and absence of remedial intent. Where deliberate omission of prāyaścitta coincides with persistent harmful behavior, the court recognizes self-imposed karmic consequence as the operative justice mechanism. Authority lies in acknowledging the natural law outcome rather than imposing punitive measures.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality confirms that unremedied harm leads to experiential consequence through sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ). Responsibility is proportional to awareness and choice. The system operates non-punitively—consequences arise organically from misalignment, not as imposed suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate consciousness recalibration through mandatory exposure to resultants of actions.
Assign completion process involving direct restitution or equivalent dharmic service.
Implement integrity reintegration via guided prāyaścitta protocols until alignment is restored.
Deploy capacity restoration modules to prevent recurrence through elevated discriminative awareness.
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Dharma. Justice flows from consciousness itself; there is no punisher, only consequence. Dharma is restored when alignment is regained. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness is the supreme adjudicator.
